name: AWS SQS/SNS
description: Protects against destructive AWS SQS and SNS operations like deleting queues, \ purging messages, deleting topics, and removing subscriptions.

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sqs-delete-queue
destructive_patterns.description: aws sqs delete-queue permanently deletes an SQS queue.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an SQS queue removes the queue and all messages in it. Messages \ in flight are lost, and any applications sending to this queue will \ receive errors. You must wait 60 seconds before recreating a queue \ with the same name.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sqs get-queue-attributes: Review queue metrics first \ - aws sqs purge-queue: Remove messages but keep the queue \ - Use message retention period for automatic cleanup

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sqs-purge-queue
destructive_patterns.description: aws sqs purge-queue deletes ALL messages in the queue.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Purging an SQS queue deletes all messages immediately. This includes \ messages in flight and delayed messages. The operation cannot be undone. \ You can only purge a queue once every 60 seconds.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sqs get-queue-attributes: Check message count first \ - Process messages normally instead of purging \ - Use dead-letter queues for failed messages

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sqs-delete-message-batch
destructive_patterns.description: aws sqs delete-message-batch removes multiple messages from the queue.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Batch deletion removes up to 10 messages at once. Messages must be \ successfully processed before deletion, or they will be lost. Ensure \ your processing logic is complete before calling delete.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Verify receipt handles are still valid \ - Use visibility timeout to prevent duplicate processing \ - Delete messages only after confirmed processing

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sqs-delete-message
destructive_patterns.description: aws sqs delete-message removes a message from the queue.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a message removes it permanently from the queue. Only delete \ after successful processing. If processing fails after deletion, the \ message is lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Extend visibility timeout if processing takes longer \ - Use dead-letter queues for failed processing \ - Implement idempotent processing for safety

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sns-delete-topic
destructive_patterns.description: aws sns delete-topic removes an SNS topic and its subscriptions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an SNS topic removes all subscriptions and stops all message \ delivery. Publishers will receive errors. Lambda functions, SQS queues, \ and other subscribers will no longer receive notifications.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic: Review subscribers first \ - Unsubscribe endpoints individually if needed \ - Use topic policies to restrict publishing instead

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sns-unsubscribe
destructive_patterns.description: aws sns unsubscribe removes a subscription and stops message delivery.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Unsubscribing stops message delivery to that endpoint. If this is a \ critical integration (Lambda, SQS, HTTP endpoint), that system will \ stop receiving notifications immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sns get-subscription-attributes: Review subscription first \ - Use subscription filter policies to reduce traffic \ - Disable the endpoint instead of unsubscribing

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sns-remove-permission
destructive_patterns.description: aws sns remove-permission revokes permissions on a topic.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing permissions can break cross-account access or service \ integrations. AWS services and other accounts may lose the ability \ to publish or subscribe to the topic.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sns get-topic-attributes: Review current policy first \ - Add new permissions before removing old ones \ - Use IAM policies for fine-grained access control

destructive_patterns.name: aws-sns-delete-platform-application
destructive_patterns.description: aws sns delete-platform-application removes a platform application.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a platform application removes all endpoints and stops push \ notifications to mobile devices. All registered device tokens are \ removed, and users will stop receiving push notifications.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws sns list-endpoints-by-platform-application: Review endpoints \ - Disable individual endpoints instead of deleting the app \ - Back up endpoint ARNs before deletion
